title: What if toilets didn't exist?
premise: Every toilet and sewer on Earth disappears at once.

beats.caption: Every toilet on Earth vanishes. Including the one you were about to use.
Offices, schools and malls suddenly have nowhere for anyone to go.
Parks, alleys and bushes become the only option.

stat.label: PEOPLE NEED TO GO EVERY DAY

beats.caption: Cities of millions have no way to get rid of their waste.
The first heavy rain washes it all into rivers, lakes and drinking water.

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: 1854: John Snow traced a deadly London cholera outbreak to one water pump contaminated by sewage.

beats.caption: This is exactly how cholera spreads.
Hospitals fill up with diseases most countries forgot about.

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: In 1858, sewage in the Thames caused 'The Great Stink' and forced London to build modern sewers.

beats.caption: The smell alone would make big cities almost unlivable.

stat.label: PEOPLE ALREADY LACK SAFELY MANAGED SANITATION (WHO/UNICEF)

beats.caption: For billions of people, this isn't a what-if.

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: In a 2007 BMJ poll, sanitation was voted the greatest medical milestone since 1840.

beats.caption: The toilet may have saved more lives than any medicine.
